summary: Elevated 5xx rates from multipart streaming requests: header-parsing stall triggering API gateway 5xx and runtime thread freeze
description:
Issue summary:
Customers observed a sustained increase in 5xx errors originating at the API gateway during large multipart streaming requests that included unusually large custom metadata headers. Impact: multiple streaming sessions failed with 502/503 and the serving-runtime pool for the affected tenant entered a thread-spin / high CPU state, causing progressive upstream failures and client timeouts.

Impact:
- LatticeHealth reported 12% of streaming calls failing with 502/503 between 2026-03-10T02:15 and 2026-03-10T03:40 (us-west).
- Elevated p50/p95 stream latencies and increased runtime CPU usage on 6 hosts in the dedicated tenant pool.
- Customer-facing sessions reported reconnect loops; some clients retried aggressively leading to amplified load.

Environment:
- prod | us-west (tenant: lattice-prod-dedicated)
- API Gateway (nginx-based front proxy), ingress parsing pipeline -> runtime proxy -> serving-runtime GPU workers.

Steps to reproduce (internal reproduction):
1) Send a multipart streaming request simulating client behavior: a 10MB payload split into chunks with ~200 custom metadata headers (each ~16KB).
2) Observe ingress accept log; API gateway stalls while parsing headers.
3) Requests either timeout at the gateway (502) or are forwarded but cause serving-runtime request handler threads to enter long spin cycles trying to read/assemble headers, producing high CPU and watchdog resets.

Logs & Observations:
- apigw error logs: "ingress: header parse delay > 1200ms, connection queued" (see apigw-logs lines: apigw-usw-12: /var/log/apigw/2026-03-10.log:line 4872).
- runtime syslogs: recurrent "request-handler: waiting on header assembly" and then "worker watchdog triggered" followed by runtime restart entries.
- tracing: distributed trace shows 90th percentile time spent in ingress header-parsing span (ingress.parse_headers) increased from ~3ms to ~1.2s for affected requests.
- metrics: p50 latency for streaming route increased from 140ms -> 420ms; 5xx rate jump to 12% for tenant.

Investigation notes:
- Initial hypothesis was a malformed chunk boundary or backend prefetch causing backpressure; however packet captures and trace spans showed the dominant delay in header parsing at the gateway layer.
- The specific trigger was a combination of high count of headers with large individual header sizes (common when clients attach extensive per-chunk metadata). The gateway's header parser used an O(n^2) path when handling very large header maps under the current config, which isn't exercised by normal traffic.
- While header parsing was stalled, connection accept backlog increased, and proxy worker threads held file descriptors open waiting for parse completion; downstream runtime handlers received partially-assembled requests and stalled while blocking on header assembly, leading to CPU spin and eventual watchdog resets.
- Reproduced locally with a synthetic client. Confirmed that reducing header count/size avoided the condition immediately.

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Rate-limited the tenant's streaming route from the edge to reduce retry amplification (applied 2026-03-10T03:00).
- Added a temporary header count and aggregate header size limit at the API gateway layer for the tenant (soft reject with 413 when exceeded).
- Advised customer to stop including per-chunk large metadata and to aggregate metadata into the first chunk while we deploy a fix.

Root cause:
- An inefficient header parsing code path in the API gateway that degenerates under very large header counts/sizes, combined with downstream runtime handlers that assume quick header assembly and block on partial reads. This produced a feedback loop: parse stalls -> accept backlog -> proxy threads held -> serving-runtime threads blocked -> watchdogs restart -> 5xx wave.

Resolution & rollout notes:
- Patch deployed to API gateway ingress parser to short-circuit pathological header maps, move to linear-time parsing for header counts, and enforce configurable header parsing timeouts. Deployed 2026-03-11 01:30 UTC to canary pool and 2026-03-11 03:10 UTC to prod us-west.
- Serving-runtime patched to avoid blocking request handlers on header assembly by offloading header reads to async parsing goroutine and adding a parse timeout guard. Deployed 2026-03-11 02:45 UTC.
- Per-tenant soft header size/count limit implemented with clear 413 response and reason message.
- Rolling restart of 6 affected runtime hosts completed 2026-03-11 04:00 UTC.
- Post-deploy monitoring: 5xx rate for lattice-prod-dedicated returned to baseline (<0.5%) within one hour of full rollout.

Follow-ups / Action items:
- (ENG-5123) Add unit+fuzz tests for header parser edge cases (assigned to ingress team).
- (SRE-2981) Add circuit-breaker alert for ingress header-parse latency > 200ms sustained across hosts.
- Customer communication: CS sent detailed incident summary and recommended client changes.

Related links:
- Slack thread: #support-lattice / thread TS12345
- Traces: https://tracing.redwood.internal/trace/abcd-parse-span-20260310 (internal)
- Apigw logs excerpt: s3://redwood-logs/apigw/us-west/2026-03-10/apigw-usw-12.log:4872-4910
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingress/pull/2345, https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/447

resolution: Ingress parser and serving-runtime fixes deployed; tenant soft-limits applied; rolling restart completed. 5xx rates returned to baseline. Follow-up tickets created for tests and alerts.
